evidence.snippet: aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC) is the rate-limiting enzyme in the conversion of L-DOPA (Sinemet) to dopamine (DA)
evidence.explanation: Levodopa is the substrate for AADC (DDC), the enzyme that converts it to dopamine. The enzyme activity is the key step in levodopa's mechanism.

paper.title: Depletion of AADC activity in caudate nucleus and putamen of Parkinson's disease patients; implications for ongoing AAV2-AADC gene therapy trial.

evidence.snippet: Replenishment of dopamine by oral supplementation of its precursor, the levodopa (L-DOPA), remains the primary mode of treatment of PD
evidence.explanation: Levodopa is converted to dopamine in the brain, replenishing dopamine levels in Parkinson's disease patients.

paper.title: Garcinol, an effective monoamine oxidase-B inhibitor for the treatment of Parkinson's disease.

evidence.snippet: Dopamine, the major neurotransmitter depleted in Parkinson disease, can be synthesized and regulated in vivo with a combination of intrastriatal AAV-hAADC gene therapy and administration of the dopamine precursor l-Dopa.
evidence.explanation: Confirms levodopa is a dopamine precursor and its conversion to dopamine is central to its therapeutic effect.

paper.title: Long-term clinical improvement in MPTP-lesioned primates after gene therapy with AAV-hAADC.
paper.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy

evidence.snippet: Although the resulting dopamine deficiency is the cause of the typical motor features of Parkinson's disease (bradykinesia, rigidity, tremor)
evidence.explanation: Dopamine deficiency underlies Parkinson's motor symptoms; replenishment of dopamine (from levodopa) restores stimulation of dopamine receptors including DRD2, which modulates motor control.

paper.title: Monoamine oxidase B inhibitors for the treatment of Parkinson's disease: a review of symptomatic and potential disease-modifying effects.

evidence.snippet: a decrease in dopamine levels in the striatum causes abnormal circuit activity in the basal ganglia, resulting in increased output via the substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr)
evidence.explanation: Depletion of dopamine disrupts basal ganglia activity; restoration of dopamine by levodopa acts through dopamine receptors to normalize this circuit.

paper.title: Amino acid transporter Asc-1 (SLC7A10) expression is altered in basal ganglia in experimental Parkinsonism and L-dopa-induced dyskinesia model mice.

evidence.snippet: l-DOPA treatment ameliorated PD signs, particularly akinesia/bradykinesia, and normalized cortically evoked responses in both the GPi and GPe
evidence.explanation: L-DOPA directly ameliorates the motor signs of Parkinson's disease by restoring dopaminergic signaling in the basal ganglia.

paper.title: Altered Dynamic Information Flow through the Cortico-Basal Ganglia Pathways Mediates Parkinson's Disease Symptoms.

evidence.snippet: The most effective treatment for this disease continues to be the dopamine replacement therapy with levodopa together with an inhibitor of aromatic amino acid decarboxylase (AADC)
evidence.explanation: Levodopa is the gold-standard treatment for Parkinson's disease.

paper.title: Catechol-O-methyltransferase and its inhibitors in Parkinson's disease.
